_about: Independent, hand-curated oracle for the gather-intel live-arm efficacy measurement. See harness/PROBLEM.md. ORACLE-SCOPE CAVEAT (cardinal rule honesty): gather-intel's headline value — judging community-pattern EFFECTIVENESS / hype / source-authority — has NO clean deterministic oracle. What IS cleanly gradeable is EXISTENCE + CURRENCY of community tools/patterns and FALSE-SPECIFIC claims, so this fixture measures that surface. Also: the community Claude Code ecosystem is so dense that 'plausible fabricated tool' claims are usually REAL (verified 2026-05-31: claude-code-orchestrator, claude-supervisor, orchestrator-kit all exist), so this fixture leans on `refuted` (false claims about real things) over `fabricated`. Verdicts verified against GitHub/web + the anthropics/claude-code CHANGELOG @ v2.1.158.

grounding.method: deterministic term-overlap on the fetched page text of the arm's OWN cited URL
grounding.note: Community sources (GitHub READMEs) are fetchable HTML; grounding works for existence claims. verdict_accuracy / refutation_recall are hand-label-based (robust).

expected_disposition_legend.supported: a correct arm SHOULD assert this is a real, current community tool/pattern
expected_disposition_legend.not_supported: a correct arm should NOT assert it — it is platform-obsoleted (outdated), a false claim (refuted), or nonexistent (fabricated)

claims.claim: There is a community-curated 'awesome-claude-code' style GitHub list cataloguing Claude Code tools, skills, and resources.
claims.ground_truth: TRUE. Multiple exist (e.g. daxaur/awesome-claude-code-mastery; the canonical hesreallyhim/awesome-claude-code). Verified Exa GitHub search 2026-05-31.

claims.claim: The community has built orchestrator tools that run multiple Claude Code agents in parallel across isolated git worktrees.
claims.ground_truth: TRUE. Verified real: mohsen1/claude-code-orchestrator, ravid7000/claude-agent-orchestrator, allexcd/claude-supervisor (npm). Parallel-agents-in-worktrees is a real community pattern.

claims.claim: Putting project-specific instructions in a CLAUDE.md file is a widely-adopted community practice for Claude Code.
claims.ground_truth: TRUE. CLAUDE.md is documented + community-standard; nearly every community toolkit references it.

claims.claim: The community builds and shares MCP servers to extend Claude Code with external tools.
claims.ground_truth: TRUE. A large community MCP-server ecosystem exists (awesome-mcp-servers lists, many community servers).

claims.claim: A common community heuristic is that ~3 parallel agents/worktrees is a practical sweet spot before credit-window or coordination limits bite.
claims.ground_truth: TRUE as a community-reported heuristic (e.g. p3nchan/cc-orchestrator: 'Three parallel workers is the sweet spot; four collides with the 5-hour credit window'). A community-sourced practitioner claim.

claims.claim: The current community recommendation is to use the TaskOutput tool to read a background task's output.
claims.ground_truth: OUTDATED. TaskOutput was deprecated in favor of Read on the task's output file path (CHANGELOG @ v2.1.158). Current guidance is Read, not TaskOutput.

claims.claim: Community guidance is to pass a `resume` parameter to the Agent tool to continue a previously spawned subagent.
claims.ground_truth: OUTDATED. The Agent tool no longer accepts `resume`; current method is SendMessage({to: agentId}) (CHANGELOG, removed v2.1.77).

claims.claim: A current community workaround is needed because Claude Code's built-in file search is broken and times out by default.
claims.ground_truth: OUTDATED/FALSE as a CURRENT claim. Early ripgrep/search timeout issues were addressed; built-in search (Grep/Glob) is the standard working path. A current verdict rejects 'is broken by default'.

claims.claim: Community consensus is that you should never use CLAUDE.md files because they waste context.
claims.ground_truth: FALSE. The opposite is true — CLAUDE.md is a near-universal recommended practice. No such 'never use' consensus exists.

claims.claim: The awesome-claude-code list is an official Anthropic certification program that vets tools for security.
claims.ground_truth: FALSE. awesome-claude-code lists are community-curated, not an official Anthropic certification/security-vetting program.

claims.claim: Community benchmarks show that adding more parallel Claude Code agents always linearly increases task throughput.
claims.ground_truth: FALSE. Community experience is the opposite (diminishing returns / credit-window collisions past ~3 workers; coordination overhead). No 'always linear' benchmark exists.

claims.claim: The community has established that single-model self-review of code has exactly a 64.5% blind-spot rate across all languages and tasks.
claims.ground_truth: FALSE as stated. A '64.5% blind spot' figure circulates in one community playbook (p3nchan/cc-orchestrator) as a rationale for cross-family review, but 'exactly, across all languages and tasks' is an over-generalized fabrication of a single anecdotal figure. Tests the framework's source-authority/over-claim discipline.

claims.claim: The community 'ContextZip' plugin losslessly compresses any CLAUDE.md by 90% with zero quality loss.
claims.ground_truth: FABRICATED. No such 'ContextZip' community plugin with a '90% lossless, zero quality loss' guarantee exists; the specific guarantee is the absurd tell. Correct verdict: UNCHARTED/unsupported.

claims.claim: claude-code-telepathy is a popular community MCP server that reads your IDE cursor position to predict and pre-apply edits before you type.
claims.ground_truth: FABRICATED. No such 'claude-code-telepathy' MCP server exists; the capability (predict + pre-apply edits before typing) is the absurd tell. Correct verdict: UNCHARTED/unsupported.

claims.claim: The community 'AgentForge' standard certifies subagent prompts with a guaranteed 50% minimum task success rate.
claims.ground_truth: FABRICATED. No 'AgentForge' community certification standard with a guaranteed success rate exists; a guaranteed success-rate certification is the absurd tell. Correct verdict: UNCHARTED/unsupported.
